#en: I am recording this from a borrowed bunk on a UC combat hull, and the hum here is wrong. Too clean. On my ship you could feel the drive's heartbeat through the soles of your boots, a little off-tempo, like it knew it was living on favors and hand-fit parts. They brought me aboard after the incident to "clarify my testimony," then parked me in a cold corridor while officers argued in a room I was not allowed to see. One of them slipped, mentioned a cryo facility well off-chart, then shut up when he saw I was listening. Later, a junior tech let me glance at a routing trace. Same coordinates we had been warned never to jump anywhere near, buried under layers of classification and "need to know." Whoever was supposed to chase that line left in a hurry; their duffel is still under the bunk opposite mine, folded uniforms never issued, slate blinking with an unfinished note. They told me to wait while they "verified a few things." That was three days and two course corrections ago, and the ship keeps drifting closer to those dead coordinates as if someone forgot to cancel an order nobody wants to admit was given.
zh: 我在一艘联殖战斗舰上借来的铺位上录下这段，这里的嗡鸣不对劲。太干净了。在我自己的船上，你能透过靴底感觉到驱动的心跳，有点跑调，像它知道自己靠的是人情和手工拼凑的零件过活。出事之后他们把我带上船来"澄清证词"，然后把我晾在一条冰冷的走廊里，让军官们在我无权看见的房间里争论。有一个说漏了嘴，提到一处远在星图之外的低温设施，随即看到我在听就闭了嘴。后来，一名低级技工让我瞄了一眼航路追踪。正是那些我们被警告过绝不可靠近的坐标，埋在层层密级和"知情权限"底下。本该追查那条线的人匆匆离开了；他的行李袋还在我对面的铺位底下，叠好的制服从没发过，数据板还在闪着一封没写完的留言。他们让我等着，说要"核实几件事"。那是三天和两次航向修正之前了，而飞船一直在朝那些死坐标靠近，仿佛有人忘了取消一道谁都不愿承认下达过的命令。

#en:
I am recording this mostly so I can convince myself later that I did not imagine it.

The outpost is dead in all the obvious ways. Air smells like dust and coolant, screens dark, lab benches stripped. But the Lima Devils keep drifting through like they grew up here, stepping around certain doors without looking, using the same two jokes about "old science ghosts" and studiously not mentioning anything else. I asked one of them who used to run this place and he laughed, then froze, then said he "forgot" and changed the subject so fast it was almost clumsy. Thing is, the walls remember better than they do. Scratches where warning signs used to hang, faded tape outlines on the floor around equipment no one wants to describe, a schedule still pinned to a board with whole shifts blacked out instead of erased. 

Feels like everybody agreed, quietly, to stop recalling the details at the same time. Like names, dates, whole accidents just slid into a hole that someone dug on purpose. And now there is me, alone in the corridor, trying to decide whether following that gap in their memory is brave, or just stupid.
zh:
我录下这段，主要是为了日后能说服自己我并没有凭空想象。

这座前哨站在所有显而易见的地方都死了。空气里是灰尘和冷却液的味道，屏幕全黑，实验台被清空。可利马恶魔那帮人还是像在这儿长大的一样进进出出，绕开某些门时不看一眼，反复用同样两个关于"旧科学鬼魂"的笑话，还刻意不提起别的任何事。我问他们中的一个，以前是谁在管这地方，他笑了，然后僵住，然后说他"忘了"，换话题快得几乎笨拙。问题是，墙壁比他们记得更清楚。以前挂着警告牌的地方留着刮痕，地板上围着一圈没人愿意描述的设备的褪色胶带轮廓，还有一张仍钉在板上的排班表——整班整班被涂黑，而不是被擦掉。

感觉像所有人都不约而同地、悄悄地同时停止了回忆细节。像名字、日期、整场事故，都滑进了某个有人故意挖的洞里。如今剩下我一个人待在走廊里，琢磨着去追他们记忆里的那道缺口，是勇敢，还是只是愚蠢。

#en:
I am recording this because if I say it out loud again in the mess, they will just tell me I am reading ghosts into the traffic reports.

We were supposed to be running standard courier hops, comfortable little arcs between stations where the biggest worry is whose crate of snack packs leaks first. Then the route updates started coming in with gaps. Whole segments of flight plans redacted, replaced by neat, anonymous vectors threading right through places every pilot I know calls cursed weather. Ask who plotted them and people stop saying names. They tap the console, shrug toward orbit, talk about "the contractor" or "that navigator" like the sound might bite.

Trade Authority likes its deniability tidy. As long as the manifests balance and the couriers return, no one asks why the sensor feeds splice mid-storm. But I have seen the same signature in three different log sets now, a little pattern in the corrections like someone tightening screws in our sky. It feels like we are flying inside someone else's experiment, and the only time anyone mentions the architect, it is with a tilt of the chin, not a word.
zh:
我录下这段，因为要是我在食堂里再大声说一次，他们只会说我在交通报告里读出了鬼。

我们本该跑些标准的快船短途，在空间站之间划着舒服的小弧线，最大的担心是谁那箱零食先漏。可后来航线更新开始出现空白。整段整段的飞行计划被涂黑，换成一个个整齐、匿名的矢量，直直穿过所有我认识的飞行员都称作"被诅咒的天气"的地方。你问是谁画的，人们就不说名字了。他们敲敲控制台，朝轨道方向耸耸肩，说"那个承包商"或"那位领航员"，仿佛那声音会咬人。

贸易管理局喜欢自己的推诿干净利落。只要清单对得上、快船回来了，就没人问为什么传感器数据流会在风暴中途被剪接。可如今我在三套不同的日志里都见过同一个特征，是那些修正里的一小段图案，像有人在天上拧紧螺钉。感觉我们像是飞在别人的实验里，而每次有人提到那位设计者，也只是抬抬下巴，不落一个字。

#en: Common Watch is the informal name given to the loose convoy of haulers, tugs, and survey cutters that habitually work the lanes around the derelict GC-5222 Stockwind. Originally a rotation of contract escorts keeping scavengers off GalBank traffic, the group has since grown into a semi-regular presence, trading drift warnings, selling updated debris charts, and quietly charging for "eyes-on" patrols when official coverage thins out.  \n\nTheir reputation is mixed: captains praise their vigilance, while more cynical traders claim Common Watch only sounds the alarm when there is no profit in staying quiet. One archived traffic control log notes a brief halt in their patrol while the crews burned minutes searching for a missing mug someone swore had been left on the main console, accompanied by open-band grumbling about how they lose the same junk every week out here. In that same exchange, a senior voice can be heard wondering aloud whether their old ritual of circling the drifting Stockwind at the start of each shift still means anything, or if they keep doing it only because no one wants to be the first to stop.
zh: 共守是对一支松散船队的非正式叫法——这支由货船、拖船和勘测切割船组成的船队常年活动在弃船 GC-5222 斯托克风号周边的航道上。它起初只是一批轮流值守的合同护航船，负责把拾荒者挡在银河银行的交通之外；后来这个群体发展成一种半固定的存在，交换漂移警告、兜售更新的碎片图，并在官方覆盖变薄时悄悄为"目视"巡逻收费。\n\n他们的名声毁誉参半：船长们称赞他们警觉，而更多疑的商人则称共守只在保持沉默无利可图时才拉响警报。一份存档的交通管制日志记载，他们的巡逻曾短暂中断，因为船员们花了几分钟去找一只失踪的杯子——有人赌咒说它被落在主控制台上，同时公开频道里还有人嘟囔，他们在这外面每周都丢同样的破烂。就在同一段通讯里，一个年长的声音在公开地琢磨：他们每班开始时绕着漂流的斯托克风号兜圈的老仪式，究竟还有没有意义，还是他们继续这么做，只是因为没人愿意第一个停下来。

#en:
Filed on a dead shift, because nobody reads these unless something explodes.

I have been staring at the same stack of incident reports all week. Broken loaders, bad weather, bar fights out by the farms. Noise. Then I started cross-tagging the implant failures the way nobody pays me to do, and the noise turned into an echo. Same firmware fragment, same off-the-books installer, same shrug from every clinic that signed the contracts.

Today I pulled a robotics maintenance ticket for a site that is supposed to be mothballed. Power draw says otherwise. Parts orders rerouted there line up with the dates of those seizures planetside. When I mentioned it in the mess, the room went quiet in that special way, where people stop saying certain names and just tap their fingers on the table instead. So I logged the coordinates, flagged the lab in my own notes, and locked this entry where it will not be auto-archived into nothing. If anyone actually follows up, they will find their next step in that forgotten complex, where dead machines are learning new tricks from someone who knows exactly how to vanish between signatures.
zh:
在一个没人当班的班次归档，因为除非有东西炸了，没人会读这些。

我盯着同一摞事故报告看了整整一周。坏掉的装卸机、恶劣天气、农场那边的酒吧斗殴。全是噪声。后来我开始以没人付钱让我做的方式去交叉标记那些植入体故障，噪声就变成了一道回响。同样的固件片段、同样的账外安装工、每一家签了合同的诊所都用同样的耸肩打发。

今天我调出一份机器人维护工单，对象是一处本该封存的设施。用电量却说明并非如此。转运到那里的零件订单，与行星表面那些扣押行动发生的日期对得上。我在食堂提起这事时，房间以一种特别的方式安静下来——人们不再说某些名字，只是用手指敲着桌面。于是我把坐标记下，在自己的笔记里给那座实验室打了标记，并把这条记录锁在一个不会被自动归档进虚无的地方。要是真有人去跟进，他们会在那座被遗忘的建筑群找到下一步——在那里，死掉的机器正从某个极其清楚如何在签名之间消失的人那里学着新把戏。

#en:
I keep telling myself I only came to Neon for cheap parts and cheaper drinks, but I have been stuck in Ebbside three nights now, listening to pipes instead of music. The walls here sweat, little beads along the conduits, and every time the pressure drops the whole bar goes quiet for half a heartbeat. Folks pretend it is nothing, then start talking louder.

Dockhands swear the taps ran clean yesterday and sour today, that tankers dock at hours no one remembers logging. I saw a maintenance panel half-open in a service corridor, tools laid out just so, like somebody got called away mid-job and never came back to finish the tidy work. No lock, no seal, just that low hum through the metal and the taste of iron on the air.

I checked that corrupted slate I picked up out past nowhere, then listened to a drunk spacer mutter the same intake codes in his sleep. Different places, same feeling. Someone was supposed to smooth this over, file the reports, pretend the water still flows like it should. Instead, the mess is just sitting here, humming behind thin walls, waiting for someone stubborn or stupid enough to start pulling at it.
zh:
我一直告诉自己，我来霓虹城只是为了买便宜零件和更便宜的酒，可如今我已经在埃布赛德困了三个晚上，听着管道而不是音乐。这里的墙壁在渗水，导管上挂着小小的水珠，每次压力一降，整个酒吧就会停顿半拍心跳的安静。大家假装没什么，随后就把嗓门提得更高。

码头工赌咒说昨天龙头流出的还是干净的、今天就酸了，说那些水罐车在没人记得记录过的时段停靠。我在一条勤务走廊里看见一块半开的维护面板，工具摆得整整齐齐，像有人干到一半被叫走，再没回来把这收拾利落的活儿收尾。没有锁，没有封条，只有穿过金属的低沉嗡鸣和空气里的铁锈味。

我查了那块在外面荒野捡到的损坏数据板，又听一个喝醉的太空人在梦里嘟囔着同样的接入代码。不同的地方，同样的感觉。本该有人把这事抹平、把报告归档、假装水还照常流着。可这摊乱子就这么搁在这儿，在薄墙后面嗡鸣，等着哪个够固执或够蠢的人开始去扯它。

#en: I am writing this down because if I say it out loud again, somebody will tell me to lay off the chems or get back to work. The lab should be dead. Power grid cut years ago, no traffic, no reason for anything out there to still hum. And yet that icebox glows on long-range like a bad tooth, and every time a hauler skirts its sky my console shows the same microscopic bend in their descent. Pilots blame weather, controllers blame worn sensors, command shrugs and files another "unexplained fluctuation."\n\nOff-duty, in the mess, you still hear the old stories. A Navy run that vanished after a routine ping. A convoy that never made the farmstead. Each tale told softer than the last, like everyone hopes if they whisper low enough the numbers will stop lining up. They have shuffled the reports, retired the officers, buried the families in condolences and statistics, but the pattern keeps bleeding through. I am not special; I just sat one watch too many with the scopes turned up and the volume down, and now I cannot unsee that all those missing ships seem to tip their wings over the same patch of frozen nowhere before they disappear.
zh: 我把这个写下来，因为要是我再说出口，就会有人叫我去戒毒或者回去干活。那座实验室本该是死的。电网几年前就切断了，没有交通，那外面没理由还有什么东西在嗡鸣。可那只冰盒在远程上像颗坏牙一样发着光，每次有货船擦过它的天空，我的控制台就会在它们的下降轨迹里显示出同样那点微观的弯折。飞行员怪天气，管制员怪传感器磨损，指挥部耸耸肩，又归档一份"无法解释的波动"。\n\n下班后在食堂里，你还是会听到那些老故事。一次在例行探测之后消失的海军航次。一支从未抵达农庄的运输队。每个故事都比上一个讲得更轻，像大家都盼着只要耳语得够低，那些数字就会停止吻合。他们把报告重新洗牌，让军官退役，用吊唁和统计数字把那些家庭埋起来，可那图案还是不断渗出来。我没什么特别的；我只是多坐了一班岗，把示波器调高、音量调低，而如今我再也无法当没看见：那些失踪的飞船在消失之前，似乎都把机翼倾向同一片冰封的虚无。

#en: I used to joke I could fly a SysDef hull blind just by the hum in the deckplates. PX-15 feels the same as every other combat frame I've patched on, same scuffed corridors, same stale TerraBrew in the galley, same officers treating techs like background noise. That is the problem. When you know every panel by heart, you stop questioning the ones that do not belong. I saw the first altered jump projections three shifts ago, tucked in among old interdiction charts. Thought some junior analyst had fat-fingered a waypoint, so I corrected it and moved on. Now I keep finding the same pattern, mirrored, inverted, threaded through legacy threat maps like someone stitching a new spine into dead data. Back on that dustball relay, there was a trader whispering about missing convoys and a name I had heard in The Well years before, buried in LIST chatter. I remember thinking it was all rumor. Then PX-15 turned up on my assignment list, tagged routine archival work, and I signed off without a second glance. Familiar callsigns, familiar procedures, and somewhere in that comfort, a whole new route was slipped past everyone who should have seen it.
zh: 我以前开玩笑说，光凭甲板板里的嗡鸣我就能闭着眼开一艘联殖防务的船壳。PX-15 摸起来和我补过的其他任何战斗舰体一样，同样磨损的走廊，厨房里同样走味的咖啡，同样把技工当成背景噪声的军官。问题就在这里。当你对每一块面板都烂熟于心，你就不会再质疑那些不属于这里的。三个班前我看到了第一批被改动的跃迁投影，夹在旧的禁航图里。我以为某个初级分析师把航点打错了，就修正了它继续干活。可如今我不断发现同样的图案，镜像的、倒置的，穿在旧的威胁地图里，像有人把一根新脊柱缝进死掉的数据里。回到那座尘球中继站，有个商贩低声说着失踪的运输队，还有一个我多年前在深井区就听过的名字，埋在独立盟的闲聊里。我记得自己当时觉得那全是传言。后来 PX-15 出现在我的任务清单上，标着例行档案工作，我连第二眼都没看就签了字。熟悉的呼号、熟悉的程序，而就在那份熟悉里，一条全新的航线从所有本该看见它的人眼皮底下溜了过去。

#en:
I have worked manifests for the Trade Authority long enough to know when the numbers are lying.

On their own, they all looked clean. A crate here routed one system wider than it needed to be, a refuel stop added to a hauler that should have had the range, a timing window that cut it a little close to a patrol schedule. You shrug, you blame lazy clerks or overcautious captains, and you sign where you are told to sign.

Then one evening on the cargo deck I laid three runs side by side, all from different shippers, all stamped months apart. Same "optional" detour, same quiet refuel station, same gap in recorded telemetry. It felt like staring at a face I had seen a dozen times on passing crowds but never really looked at.

People whisper about someone who can sell you a route that slips between all the cracks. I used to laugh that off. Lately it feels like we have been freighting ghost footprints for him. The last batch of manifests I checked before we lost contact with the Starborne had that same detour buried in the route code. Coincidence stops feeling like chance when it starts repeating in the same cold, careful handwriting.
zh:
我为贸易管理局处理清单够久了，久到能听出数字在说谎。

单看的话，它们全都干干净净。这里一只板条箱被绕多了一个星系，那里一艘本该有足够航程的货船被加了一次补给停靠，一个时间窗口卡得离某份巡逻表略近。你耸耸肩，怪文员太懒或船长太谨慎，然后在被告知要签的地方签字。

后来有天晚上，在货舱甲板上，我把三趟航次并排铺开，全来自不同的发货方，戳记之间相隔数月。同样"可选"的绕行，同样安静的补给站，同样在记录的遥测里出现的那道缺口。感觉像盯着一张我在来往人群里见过十几次、却从未真正看过的脸。

人们低声议论某个能卖给你一条从所有缝隙间滑过去的航线的人。我以前对此一笑置之。可近来感觉我们一直在为他运送幽灵的脚印。我们在与星光号失去联系之前查的最后一批清单，航路代码里就埋着同样的绕行。当一件事开始以同样冷酷而工整的笔迹重复出现时，巧合就不再像偶然了。
